Good morning. It's Thursday, August 13. Here's your pre-market briefing.

Three developments stand out this morning, and I'll take them in order of how
much they can move prices. First, the inflation print. Second, the thirty-year
auction. Third, the tone of the FOMC minutes due next week.

Turning to the overnight tape. The S&P 500 closed at 7,748.50, up 0.26%. Two of
the eleven sectors closed lower. Technology led, up 1.49%.

On rates. The ten-year is at 4.68%, down 2 basis points. This is the fourth
consecutive session of lower yields, the longest such run since 2024, and the
market has now priced four consecutive quarters of disinflation.

Looking ahead. Consumer prices land at 8:30 a.m., and the thirty-year auction
follows at 1:00 p.m. There are five more sessions before the FOMC minutes.

That's your briefing. Have a good one.
